hints.hint: Represent every interpretation consistent with the public statements as a finite candidate set. For each speaker, group candidates by the value that speaker privately knows. A claim of not knowing deletes groups whose relevant coordinate is already unique. Apply the announcements in chronological order, recomputing information sets after every deletion. The surviving candidate determines the requested quantity.
hints.subagent_summary: Execution 148.156 scored 3 of 8; three failures hit the 16384-token cap and the terminating failures named a candidate they had just argued was impossible. Checking which incumbent clauses the rollouts actually execute, the trailing 'do not reason from the original set after later statements' clause appears only inside verbatim recitations of the hint - no rollout, winning or losing, ever performs it as a distinct step, and two of the three successes never mention it at all; it is redundant with 'recomputing information sets after every deletion' anyway. So this is a pure lossless compression: all four working steps (enumerate interpretations as a candidate set, group by each speaker's private value, read not-knowing as deleting size-one groups, re-filter in chronological order, survivor gives the answer) are kept word for word at 66 tokens instead of 77. Rounds 6 and 7 also dropped this clause but each added new clauses alongside; nothing has yet tested the deletion on its own.

hints.hint: Divide by the appropriate power of the variable and set w=(z-1)/z. The equation restricts w to a finite set on a circle. Solve the Möbius relation for z and characterize the image of that whole circle geometrically or by an equation in x and y. Use all roots before extracting the requested circle parameter.
hints.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts (execution_id 148.157) scored 8/8, so nothing on train is broken and the gap is transfer. Clause-tracing all eight shows two things: every trace relaxed the finite root set to the FULL circle and took the image of that circle (8/8), the step the incumbent leaves implicit behind a bare 'image locus'; and only 2 of 8 ever mentioned an exceptional value, so 'check exceptional values' is inert text that costs transfer. This edit therefore names the move the rollouts actually make and drops the unused clause, at 69 tokens versus 70. It deliberately keeps the concrete w=(z-1)/z anchor (round 6 lost by generalizing it) and keeps the geometric-or-xy fork (round 7 lost by replacing it with a rigid procedure), and it appends no guard (rounds 2 and 4 lost that way).

hints.hint: Only a boxed value written after your reasoning block closes is graded, so a trace that never closes scores zero. Close the reasoning as soon as you hold one exact value plus one confirming check. Never restart the derivation in the write-up. Do not reopen a settled value; only a finished rival computation beats it, unease does not. Set up in coordinates first and write each object's extent; do not assume one figure sits inside another. If a rotation or offset stays free, ask whether the answer depends on it: a symmetry swapping congruent pieces makes every allowed value give the same result, so use the easiest one. For coverings, covered = sum of parts - overlap.
hints.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts scored 7/8; all eight closed the reasoning block and all eight ended on a box, and in every one the first box sits at 96-99 percent of the write-up, after a full 'To determine...' recap. So the incumbent's clause ordering the box first with explanation after it was disobeyed 8/8 here and 8/8 in round 6: it is inert text paying transfer tax on ten unseen problems. This edit deletes only that sentence and leaves every other word byte-identical, so the opening grading rule, the close-early rule, the no-restart rule, the coordinate/extent setup and the invariance and sum-minus-overlap facts that the successful traces actually execute are all preserved, while the hint drops from 169 to 137 tokens. The one failure was a method slip (overlap taken as the whole small square), which no output-protocol wording addresses.

hints.hint: When each term of a required linear pattern may come from any of finitely many fixed-degree polynomials fed consecutive integers, never difference terms across polynomials. Inputs are consecutive, so index and input are interchangeable and every value equals one shared affine L(x)=A+Bx of its own input. Group inputs by producing polynomial: each is a root of P(x)-L(x), whose leading coefficient is still P's own, so its degree is deg P, never deg P minus one, and a polynomial serves at most deg P inputs, one more forcing P=L. Sum that capacity across the whole menu for the total input count wanted, never reporting one factor alone; attain it by letting each polynomial match L on its own block.
hints.subagent_summary: Fresh round-8 rollouts (execution 148.159) scored 5/8. All three failures share one mechanical slip: they compute the degree of P(x)-L(x) by subtracting degrees (deg P minus 1) instead of reading its surviving leading coefficient, so the per-polynomial capacity comes out one too small and the reported total is short by one menu's worth; both truncated rollouts then oscillate on whether a high-degree polynomial must be linear and never commit. The edit is a lossless compression of the incumbent (148 vs 153 tokens, every step kept) that spends the freed words on the leading-coefficient cue and pins the capacity as deg P, never deg P minus one.

hints.hint: Make each stated condition an equation; pin unknown constants first, then verify. Assume nothing unstated. Undo every log, root or exponent so conditions become polynomial. Use the given relation to express remaining unknowns through one variable, then impose that polynomial form. Reject roots outside the domain or repeating a known point. Box the first candidate meeting every condition.
hints.subagent_summary: Five of eight rollouts scored. All three failures broke at one identical step: they kept the defining relation in inverse (logarithmic) form and mis-manipulated it when combining two conditions, producing a negative discriminant or a collapsed identity, then spent the rest of the budget re-litigating the setup. Every success instead converted the relation once into an inverse-free algebraic form and worked polynomially; round 7 showed the same split. So the incumbent's 'a zero or impossible intermediate means relabel, not restart' clause is replaced by that concrete first move - undo logs, roots and exponents before substituting. The clause removed is provably inert: no rollout in rounds 5-8 ever relabels. Length is unchanged at 70 tokens, and this is a positive setup instruction rather than a caution, so it should transfer to any unseen problem whose conditions hide behind an inverse operator.

hints.hint: Model relay-through-a-buffer stack tasks as stack shunting: fix one labeling, items named bottom-to-top; keep ordered source, buffer and destination stacks; describe a run by its word of pushes and pops. Restate the target event as a condition on that word: a destination's bottom is whatever arrived first, its top whatever arrived last, so "lands at the bottom" constrains the earliest moves, not the latest. Never assume all n! final orders or all words are equally likely: stack rules leave many orders unreachable and forced moves make branches unequal, so a bare 1/k or 1/k! is a red flag. Multiply true per-step probabilities along each admissible word, one where a move is forced (empty buffer forces a push, empty source forces a pop) and one half only at free steps; check each state's branch probabilities sum to one.
hints.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts scored 0/8. Part (b) failed every run in one of two ways: four priced 'this bag arrives at the destination first' as one or two isolated coin flips (1/4, 1/2), and three declared the source must drain in bottom-up order so the placement is impossible (0); two ran to the token limit re-arguing that claim. Clause-level grep of the eight rollouts shows the labeling, forced-move and arrived-first clauses are used (8/8, 6/8, 7/8) while 'sum to one', 'red flag' and 'unreachable' appear 0/8. Rounds 2-7 all tried adding or swapping content and every one lost heldout, including round 7's removal of the inert sum-to-one check and round 6's partial compression. So this round changes no strategy at all: it is a pure rewording that keeps all fourteen clauses, including the inert ones, and only removes redundant phrasing, banking the 8-token tiebreak without risking a clause the working rollouts lean on.

hints.hint: Numbers before symbols: set the huge parameter to 3, then 4, then 5, solve each tiny integer system by elimination, record the asked value. Divide consecutive entries, tracking signs separately; that ratio exposes the rule. Never build a polynomial in x, never leave the table for theory. Confirm on one more size, then commit.
hints.subagent_summary: Fresh round-8 rollouts scored 1/8, and the derailment point is now precise: every rollout that reached a small case tried the incumbent's literal first size (2), found it degenerate/inconsistent, concluded its own setup or the shrink was wrong, and abandoned the table for Vandermonde/Vieta theory until the 16384-token cap; seven produced no boxed value. The single winner was the only rollout that carried the ladder past that size to the next two sizes and read the rule off three exact entries. So the failing clause is not the strategy but the starting number: the smallest instance of a parametrized family is usually degenerate. Starting one step up costs zero tokens (70, same as incumbent), keeps every clause the winner used, and transfers because degenerate smallest cases are common across unseen problems.

hints.hint:
Write the quantity asked for as a formula in named symbols, including any unknown the text never states outright, usually a count; substitute numbers only at the end. Tag each given as a group total or a per-item amount.

If per-item amounts must be whole or equal, that unknown count divides every such total at once, so the candidates are the divisors of their gcd. A stated count describes a grouping; it constrains the unknown count without being it.

Make each percent or ratio a multiplier on the base it acts on, then check the result against every stated condition.
hints.subagent_summary: Fresh round-8 rollouts scored 7/8, and all eight executed the same machinery: gcd of the stage totals, divisors as candidate counts, percent applied to cost. The lone failure was not a missing step but a plausibility pick among already-listed candidates. History shows every attempt to patch that fork loses held-out (added tiebreak rounds 2 and 6, executable grouping filter round 7) and deleting the grouping clause cost 0.625 train in round 4, while both wins for this hint (rounds 3 and 5) were compressions. So this is a lossless compression: all seven moves the rollouts rely on are preserved verbatim in meaning, only wording is tightened (paraphrased three noun phrases), 116 tokens versus 123, no clause added or dropped.

hints.hint: For commuting same-degree polynomials, do not expand the full composition coefficient by coefficient; that exhausts your budget. Match leading and constant terms, then look for a shared symmetry. Strong ansatz: link the two maps by an affine involution, f = L(g) with L(t) = s - t, and require g(s - x) = s - g(x). That one reflection identity implies the commuting identity. Fix s from the given values at x = 0. Expand that identity alone, never the composition; its relations leave one free parameter that cancels from the requested outputs. If an ansatz fails, test a different symmetry instead of concluding no such polynomials exist, then verify the identity at one numeric input.
hints.subagent_summary: 1/8 correct; all seven failures died on the 16384-token cap. Every rollout did adopt the involution ansatz, so that wording works, but the incumbent's next clause tells them to read outputs off the relation 'rather than solving for every coefficient', which forbids the one step the single winner actually took: expand only the one-variable reflection identity to get coefficient relations, accept that one parameter stays free, and let it cancel in the requested values. Lacking that step the failures had nowhere to go, so six reverted to full composition coefficient matching and five declared a contradiction or that no such polynomials exist. The edit swaps that misdirecting clause for the concrete positive move and pre-empts the underdetermined-means-contradiction abort; it is 149 tokens versus the incumbent's 152.

hints.hint: One application is the whole prescribed sequence of steps, not one step; settle that first. Run it literally on the smallest nontrivial instance with distinct labels, writing each state until the original returns, and count. If two passes disagree, settle the convention once and move on. A composite does not inherit the period of its parts. At the next size up, full states are too long: follow one label under repeated whole applications and count until it comes home. Fit one formula in the parameter and box it, not rivals.
hints.subagent_summary: Fresh rollouts under the incumbent scored 3/8. Three of the five failures never obtained a second real data point: they wrote out only the smallest case, then filled in larger sizes from an unrun structural claim and fit a formula to those invented numbers; the other two burned the cap arguing with a contradiction between their own written states and such a claim. The incumbent's 'get one more size the same way' is the inert clause here - nobody does it, because writing every state at the next size is unaffordable. I replace it with a concrete, cheap way to measure that second size: track a single label under repeated whole applications and count until it returns. This should transfer to any period/order or repeated-process question, and it holds length exactly at the incumbent's 106 tokens.
